channel.title: NBC Sports Rotoworld NFL Player News
channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: Pat Freiermuth (calf) is questionable for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Pat Freiermuth PIT Tight End

Freiermuth popped up on the injury report Saturday afternoon with a calf injury. He’s questionable for this weekend against the Buccaneers. Freiermuth would’ve been in line for a sizable workload with the Steelers down multiple wide receivers. Coming off a two touchdown performance in Week 5, fantasy managers need a backup plan in case Freiermuth is ultimately ruled out against Tampa Bay.

Source: Steelers PR Burt

item.title: DK Metcalf (illness) was removed from the injury report and is expected to play against the Buccaneers in Week 6.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

Good news. Metcalf missed practice Friday and was listed as questionable, but has since been removed from the injury report and is expected to play this week. With the Steelers missing Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek, Metcalf could see even more targets than usual against Tampa Bay.

Source: Steelers PR Burt

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is “good to go” and should be activated for Week 6 against the Browns.
item.description:
Ja'Kobi Lane BAL Wide Receiver

While nothing is official yet, Lane practiced in full all week, which is another good sign for his availability against the Browns this weekend. Lane was one of the most impressive rookies this offseason and preseason. Rashod Bateman isn’t on the injury report, but missed practice during the week with a shoulder. Lane could conceivably operate as the second option in the Ravens passing game behind Zay Flowers as early as this week.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Commanders beat writer Ben Standig reports RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) isn’t expected to play in Week 6 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

Croskey-Merritt has dealt with a groin injury all season despite playing in the Commanders’ first five games. He missed multiple practices this week and will now get two weeks off with missing the game against the 49ers ahead of Washington’s bye week. For now, expect Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler to handle the majority of the backfield touches for the Commanders.

Source: Ben Ständig

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Chargers have rejected trade calls and aren’t planning a fire sale.
item.description:
Joe Hortiz LAC Front Office

According to Pelissero, teams have called Chargers GM Joe Hortiz, but he’s not interested in potential trade offers despite Los Angeles’ 0-5 record. The Chargers have one game left before their bye week and if they lose to the 4-0 Chiefs, falling to 0-6, this could all change. For now, the Chargers GM doesn’t want to deal, but trade calls on veteran players aren’t going to stop without a massive turnaround. Pelissero mentions Khalil Mack, Bud Dupree, Daiyan Henley, Donte Jackson, Denzel Perryman, Dalvin Tomlinson, and Tuli Tuipulotu as potential trade candidates in the final year of their contracts with the Chargers. He adds that he wouldn’t be surprised if teams that need running back or receiver help call about Keaton Mitchell, Kimani Vidal, and Quentin Johnston.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) still isn’t practicing.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

The Packers play the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football on NBC and Peacock in Week 6, but Parsons still isn’t practicing. According to Pelissero, it’s unlikely the 27-year-old defensive end plays before Green Bay’s matchup with the Patriots in Week 9 at the earliest. The Packers’ defense has certainly struggled without Parsons, but they have enough offensive firepower to win shootouts, which only adds to the fantasy floor for Jordan Love and Green Bay’s skill players.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) is still a few weeks away from a return to game action.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

No surprise here. Pierce shed his cast earlier this week, but there was also a report from the Athletic’s James Boyd that he “didn’t get the sense” Pierce was close to a return. Pelissero reports that Pierce isn’t expected to return to practice next week when he’s eligible. It’s difficult to justify holding Pierce in leagues without IR spots given the circumstances.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports there’s “optimism” Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return in Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield didn’t practice this week, but according to Buccaneers HC Todd Bowles he threw on Monday and was pushing to play before his “thumb swelled up on him.” It seems like Mayfield is trending in the right direction and that he could return against the Panthers in Week 7 if the swelling is no longer an issue. Jalon Daniels is starting for Tampa Bay again in Week 6 against the Steelers.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Eagles aren’t planning to place QB Jalen Hurts (blood clot) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Jalen Hurts PHI Quarterback

While Hurts still has no timetable to return, the Eagles haven’t even discussed the possibility of placing him on injured reserve, according to Schefter. That could change as there’s still a possibility Hurts could wind up on injured reserve if that’s where the medical information leads them. Most blood clots are treated with anticoagulants (blood thinners), which would sideline Hurts for a minimum of six weeks, according to Schefter’s sources. The best-case scenario, according to Schefter, seems to be if the blood clot is minor enough that doctors could begin treatment with anti-inflammatories. Two team doctors that Schefter polled also speculated that the 28-year-old quarterback could miss six weeks. Tanner McKee is in line to start at least a few games while Hurts is out.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Ian Rapoport reports the Patriots will likely activate WR A.J. Brown (ankle) to play against the Jets in Week 6.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Brown returned to practice this week after going on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. While nothing is official yet, it’s a great sign that Rapoport is anticipating a return for the 29-year-old wide receiver in Week 6 against the Jets. Brown may not play a full complement of snaps in his first game back, but is still essentially a must-start for fantasy managers.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Titans CEO Burke Nihill said the organization fully believes in coach Robert Saleh and general manager Mike Borgonzi.
item.description:
Robert Saleh TEN Head Coach

The Titans are 0-5 and have won only three games since Borgonzi joined the team prior to the 2025 season. Despite this, Nihill told ESPN’s Turron Davenport that he feels a “sense of stability” in the organization. Davenport, in turn, notes that the Titans “have fired a coach or general manager every year since 2022.” Nihill apologized to Titans fans, saying ownership and team executives feel “a sense of grief” about the endless losses, and “feel the sense of responsibility to deliver” for fans moving forward. We wish them luck.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Caleb Williams (hamstring) posted a video to social media indicating he will play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

Normally, social media posts don’t count for much. However, earlier today, Bears coach Ben Johnson said that the Bears should have more clarity on Williams’ status by the end of the day, after the medical team put Williams through “the final stress tests” in his return-to-play program. We are inferring that Williams’ social media post suggests he passed the final medical testing, though we have not officially received word that this is indeed the case. For now, we tentatively expect Williams to play on Sunday. He can be treated as a mid-to-low QB1.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the NFL “could step back in and create a longer suspension” for Josh Jacobs if the video showing his altercation with a woman is released.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Fowler is surprisingly saying the quiet part out loud here, though this has been the general consensus for fans and analysts for a while. Jacobs is scheduled to come off the NFL’s Commissioner Exempt list on Monday. The NFL is reportedly trying to get hold of the video, and Jacobs has sued to block its release. Fowler adds that the woman’s attorney said her client has not participated in the league’s investigation due to privacy concerns. If the video stays under wraps, Jacobs could be allowed to continue playing in the NFL.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Eagles will decide whether to place Jalen Hurts (blood clot) on short-term injured reserve on Saturday.
item.description:
Jalen Hurts PHI Quarterback

Fowler reportedly spoke to “some people who are hopeful” that Hurts can avoid injured reserve. He described the situation as being “very much touch and go” and said Tanner McKee will “probably” start multiple games. The Eagles go on bye in Week 10, so if Hurts does land on injured reserve, the Eagles’ Week 11 game against the Steelers would be his earliest possible return.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Christian Kirk (calf) was limited on Friday.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

Kirk’s inability to practice fully despite his lengthy injured reserve stint suggests he might need another week or two to get ready for an NFL game. Still, the 49ers don’t face the Commanders until Monday night. If active, he could end up warranting FLEX treatment with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) ailing.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Nick Bosa (calf) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive Lineman

Bosa is on the wrong side of questionable despite prior reports and coaching comments indicating he has a chance to face the Commanders on Monday night. For now, we expect Bosa to miss another week, though the extra day off could help him return.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Even for an iron man like Evans, this is a little concerning. Frankly, we still expect Evans to play, but two missed practices due partially to Achilles “soreness” are less than ideal. The 49ers face the Commanders on Monday night. Making a backup plan is worthwhile at this time.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Ashton Jeanty (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

The Raiders’ starting running back is good to go for what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment. The Raiders encouragingly stopped listing Jeanty with an ankle injury this week. Hopefully, his remaining plantar fasciitis issue subsides before long as well. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 in Week 6.

Source: Las Vegas Raiders

item.title: Brock Bowers (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

One of these days, Bowers will be removed from the injury report for good. For now, we will continue to let you know that the Raiders’ star player gets a half day on Wednesday before practicing in full for the rest of the week. Bowers is the overall TE1 in fantasy football each week. Start him accordingly.

Source: Las Vegas Raiders

item.title: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Friday.
item.description:
Austin Ekeler WAS Running Back

Ekeler continues to practice in a limited capacity while wearing a red non-contact jersey. He has a chance to play on Monday night, but he is clearly hurting. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) remains sidelined and Rachaad White (shoulder) has been downgraded to limited. It’s an ailing backfield.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

Croskey-Merritt has played through multiple injuries this year. We still think he has a chance to face the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Rachaad White (shoulder) sported a red non-contact jersey for the first time this week, and was downgraded to limited today.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Terry McLaurin (hamstring/rest) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Terry McLaurin WAS Wide Receiver

The Commanders added a “rest” designation to McLaurin’s report, so fantasy managers should not be alarmed by today’s absence. The veteran wide receiver played through the injury last week and should be expected to do so again this week. McLaurin is a WR2 against the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Ed Oliver is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Ed Oliver BUF Defensive Lineman

Bills slot CB Dee Alford (ankle) is also questionable. Coach Joe Brady said a week ago that both players avoided long-term injuries. They might actually have a chance to play this week. Stay tuned.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Joshua Palmer (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Joshua Palmer BUF Wide Receiver

Palmer practiced in a red non-contact jersey on Thursday. Even if he plays this week, he is likely only relevant in single-game DFS tournaments. He mostly provides Josh Allen with another viable target on a couple of plays.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia notes that Moore resumed practicing today after sitting out on Wednesday and Thursday. He did the same thing last week before being labeled questionable and ultimately ruled out on game day. It looks like he’s a game-time decision again this week. If active, he can be started as a WR2, but re-injury remains a risk.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Free agent Terrell Jennings worked out for the Patriots on Friday.
item.description:
Terrell Jennings

Free agent running backs Ulysses Bentley and Josh Pitsenberger also worked out for the Patriots. TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Jets. Perhaps the Patriots are making backup plans.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Elijah Arroyo (shoulder) underwent further testing on Friday.
item.description:
Elijah Arroyo SEA Tight End

No update yet on what was learned, and we may have to wait until next week’s first injury report to learn more. The Seahawks’ young tight end has faced multiple injuries in his short career. Hopefully, this one is not serious.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold’s starting quarterback job is not in jeopardy.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

The Seahawks’ head coach stood by his quarterback today, saying Darnold is “definitely part of the solution” to the offense’s recent struggles. Darnold returned somewhat quickly from a glute tendon strain a couple of weeks ago. One wonders if he is still rounding back into form following the early-season ailment. Backup Drew Lock played well in his stead, but the Seahawks believe their Super Bowl-winning quarterback should keep his job. That makes sense to us. He’s a QB2 next week against the Chiefs.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Davis Allen (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Davis Allen

He got in a limited session and the Rams apparently trust him to play despite a pair of missed practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Colby Parkinson (shoulder) also avoided the final report. Tyler Higbee is the Rams tight end you should be using at this point.

item.title: Lions placed Ben Bartch on injured reserve with a foot injury.
item.description:
Ben Bartch DET Offensive Lineman

The Lions lose one of their top backup offensive lineman and LB Devin White (forearm) to injured reserve. Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters post-game last week that White would likely require surgery.

Source: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk

item.title: Budda Baker (groin) is questionable for Arizona’s Week 6 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Budda Baker ARI Safety

It was a pop-up DNP for Baker on Friday after he had initially been listed as NIR-Rest on Wednesday. Ominous. Baker stands a real chance at missing Sunday’s game and throwing the Cardinals defense into (checking notes)

item.title: Josh Downs (hamstring/rest) is not on Indianapolis’ final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Josh Downs IND Wide Receiver

Given how Downs’ season is going, it’s hard to believe he’s going to do much with the extra runway, but Tyler Warren (groin) popping up on the report could shift more targets to Downs and Keenan Allen on Sunday against the Titans.

item.title: Tyler Warren (groin) is questionable for Indianapolis’ Week 6 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Tyler Warren IND Tight End

Warren popped up on the injury report on Friday after suffering the injury in practice. Fantasy managers who were relying on Warren likely won’t find a good enough option to replace him with proactively on waivers at this point, so it makes some sense to sit and wait for more reporting to come out or for him to be ruled out. This was, frankly, the last thing the Colts needed given how banged up their receiving corps has been.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 6 game against the Colts.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears didn’t practice Thursday but was a full-go on Friday. He’ll be a sketchy FLEX option against the Colts in Week 6 assuming he plays; it sure does seem like he will after a full session.

item.title: Eli Stowers (quad) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Eli Stowers PHI Tight End

Stowers is only notable because of his draft capital. The second-round rookie has not carved out a role for himself and would not be fantasy-relevant if the Eagles activate him from injured reserve.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Drew Kendall (knee) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Drew Kendall PHI Center

Kendall, the Eagles’ starting center, and LG Landon Dickerson (knee) were both limited on Friday, resulting in questionable game tags. Dickerson remains on injured reserve. The team would need to activate him, if he is going to play. Eagles EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle) was cleared to play.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Darnell Mooney (neck) is not on New York’s final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Darnell Mooney NYG Wide Receiver

Mooney turned seven targets into 14 yards last week and does not need to be trusted to do better this week.

item.title: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Apparently, Wicks’ day off on Thursday was only a rest day. The Eagles’ veteran wide receiver was limited on Wednesday and practiced fully today. Wicks played through the injury last week, posting a 5/63 receiving line with DeVonta Smith sidelined. Smith is back this week. Wicks is a boom-bust FLEX starter, catching passes thrown by backup Tanner McKee.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Theo Johnson (neck) will not play in New York’s Week 6 game against the Saints.
item.description:
Theo Johnson NYG Tight End

It’s Thomas Fidone hours in New York, marone.

item.title: Andrew Thomas (groin) is questionable for New York’s Week 6 game against the Saints.
item.description:
Andrew Thomas NYG Tackle

This is a marked downgrade for Thomas, as he had been skipping plenty of practice days but at least had been cleared off the injury report on Fridays the last few weeks. John Harbaugh said Thomas was “basically full go” today, which seems sketchy in light of this listing. If we take the coach at his word, it seems likely that Thomas will play through this. Ditto Jermaine Eluemunor, who also is questionable after missing the first two days of practice.

item.title: Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is questionable for Dallas’ Week 6 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Joey Porter DAL Cornerback

Porter downgraded from full to limited on Friday and wound up with this status despite practicing all three days this week. Peculiar. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson would be better off on Sunday if Porter wasn’t able to go.

item.title: Keisean Nixon (groin) is not on Green Bay’s final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Keisean Nixon GB Cornerback

He got in a pair of limited sessions on Thursday and Friday to get off the report. Nixon will be tasked with the unenviable duties of taking on George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb in front of a national audience on Sunday night.

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) is not on the final injury report for Week 6 against the Panthers.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Smith sat out on Wednesday, but practiced in a limited capacity on Thursday before upgrading to full on Friday. Smith told media members earlier today that he is “good,” and that the toe injury is not an issue. Jalen Hurts (blood clot) is out indefinitely, so Smith will be working with pocket-passing backup Tanner McKee. The Panthers are currently without both of their starting perimeter cornerbacks. It might be a bit uncomfortable, but Smith is a WR2 in Week 6.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Skyy Moore (ankle) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 6 game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Skyy Moore GB Wide Receiver

We’re Skyying less and less. Assuming Savion Williams (ankle) isn’t activated off injured reserve, J. Michael Sturdivant could become a deep-league stab or DFS punt against the Cowboys.

item.title: Eagles ruled out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

It was pretty clear that this was where things were headed when Barkley was unable to practice on Wednesday and Thursday. We do not yet know Barkley’s official Friday practice participation level, but he was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue will likely split touches this week.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Savion Williams (ankle/PUP) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 6 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Savion Williams GB Wide Receiver

Williams was limited in practice all week, making it seem like he could wait another week on the PUP list. When he does come back, the WR3 role would seem to be wide open for him after Jayden Reed’s injury. He remains a decent fantasy football stash if you have extra injured reserve spots.

item.title: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that Baker Mayfield threw on “Monday as he was pushing hard to play and the thumb swelled up on him.”
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles gets another tick in the obfuscation column. On Wednesday, Bowles told reporters that Mayfield has not resumed throwing yet. Today, Palmer tells us that Mayfield “was pushing hard to play,” and, perhaps briefly, resumed throwing on Monday. Apparently, his thumb reacted poorly. Palmer adds that Mayfield is “getting better,” but that does not necessarily mean he will be able to play next week. Stay tuned.

Source: James Palmer

item.title: Eagles placed Will Shipley (foot) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. Shipley was diagnosed with a partially torn plantar fascia and was set to miss multiple weeks per reporting, so this makes sense. By the time he comes back, Saquon Barkley should be healthy, so he’s not a must-keep in short-bench leagues.

item.title: Trey Hendrickson (finger) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Trey Hendrickson BAL Outside Linebacker

He practiced in full all week after missing the last two games following finger surgery. The Ravens’ big free-agent acquisition will be full go against the Browns in Week 6.

item.title: Andrew Vorhees (foot) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
item.description:
Andrew Vorhees BAL OFFENSIVE GUARD (SUB)

The guard got in three limited sessions, he and Emery Jones Jr. (ankle) are both questionable. Ronnie Stanley, John Simpson and Roger Rosengarten were removed from the injury report.

item.title: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
item.description:
Ja'Kobi Lane BAL Wide Receiver

Lane practiced in full all week, lending credence to the idea that he’ll be activated. Ravens coach Jesse Minter stopped short of saying Lane would play when given a chance, saying they’d “figure that out,” but said he had a great week of practice.

item.title: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

Bateman was a surprise DNP on Thursday, but got in a full session today. He remains an uninspiring FLEX option against the Browns in Week 6.

item.title: Zay Flowers (toe) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Perhaps feeling a bit wistful after spending a little of every week of the season on the injury report, Flowers got re-added Thursday with a limited session. He was limited again on Friday but is expected to play. There’s no further word on how serious this toe injury was, but he’s doing enough on the field in his limited time so far this year that nobody is seriously benching Flowers anyway.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Josh Jacobs is being removed from the NFL’s Commissioner Exempt list on Monday.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

According to Schefter, “the investigation will remain open for the NFL, so it reserves the right to add further discipline if and when warranted.” Yesterday, ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reported that the league is trying to get ahold of the video showing Jacobs’ altercation with a woman at his home. Jacobs is expected to be eligible to play in Week 7 against the Lions. The situation clearly remains in flux, but Jacobs can be stashed on fantasy football benches at this time.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Will Campbell (knee) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
item.description:
Will Campbell NE OFFENSIVE TACKLE (SUB)

Campbell injured his knee in Week 5, initially causing quite the scare. Fortunately, he was able to practice all week and has a chance to face the Jets and their talented pass-rush group in Week 6.

Source: Chad Graff

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the NFL has reinstated Broncos OLB Jonathon Cooper from the commissioner’s exempt list.
item.description:
Jonathon Cooper DEN Outside Linebacker

Cooper missed the first six games of the season while on the list, and his felony court case has been moved to after the season. It’s unclear if the league considers time served on this list as separate from a personal conduct policy violation; it’s possible Cooper faces another suspension at some point. For now, it seems the NFL is content to let him play in Week 7 despite unresolved felony assault charges and domestic violence and harassment charges.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Jets.
item.description:
Christian Gonzalez NE Cornerback

Gonzalez has not played since Week 3, but he returns in time to cover Garrett Wilson in a divisional showdown. Gonzalez primarily lines up on the perimeter, but he has taken 15 combined snaps in the slot and in the box. He could take a few reps on the inside this week, but perimeter CB2 Carlton Davis (neck) is out, so Gonzalez could be asked to simply stay out wide.

Source: Chad Graff

item.title: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is questionable for New York’s Week 6 game against the Patriots.
item.description:
Kenyon Sadiq NYJ Tight End

He did upgrade to a full practice and Aaron Glenn told reporters he expects Sadiq to play. Sadiq’s fantasy upside is well-known, but with Mason Taylor back and Omar Cooper Jr. also pushing to play, his target volume has shrunk quite a bit from some of the early-season scenarios we’ve seen. He’s likely a TE2 at this point.

item.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

The Patriots’ No. 2 running back was limited all week after being diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain. He told reporters today that he was surprised he could practice this week, and is feeling “pretty good.” If active, he will be a FLEX starter, but Rhamondre Stevenson should lead the backfield in touches.

Source: Evan Lazar

item.title: Baker Mayfield (thumb) will not play in Tampa Bay’s Week 6 game against the Steelers.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

It’ll be the Jalon Daniels show again. Mayfield did not practice at any point this week. Todd Bowles tried to tell us that it was too early to tell earlier today; it wasn’t. We’ll need to see Mayfield on the practice field next week before we think he has a real shot to play against the Panthers in Week 7.

item.title: Brenen Thompson (quad) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Brenen Thompson LAC Wide Receiver

Thompson worked three limited sessions. If active he’ll likely be a boom-bust deep-league FLEX play as the Chargers have struggled to go deep with their current offensive line situation.

item.title: Kyler Gordon (calf) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Kyler Gordon CHI Defensive Back

Gordon, the team’s starting slot cornerback, and Tyrique Stevenson (hip), the team’s No. 2 perimeter cornerback, are both questionable. Bears LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring) has been ruled out. This defense is banged up, boding positively for the Falcons’ fantasy football outlook.

Source: Chicago Bears

item.title: Derwin James (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Derwin James LAC Safety

That is back-to-back weeks of no James. Donte Jackson (hamstring) was also ruled out. We’re almost through the Chargers blurbs. We think they should just put some people on injured reserve too. Keep reading.

item.title: KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
item.description:
KeAndre Lambert-Smith LAC Wide Receiver

With Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston suiting up this week, any chance of Lambert-Smith returning to real fantasy value looks quashed. For this week, anyway. He did get in a full session today. If activated off injured reserve ahead of the contest, he can be ignored until after the Week 7 bye.

item.title: Keeanu Benton (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Keeanu Benton PIT Defensive Tackle

This is worth watching. Benton is a talented interior defender. Bucky Irving’s Week 6 outlook would be enhanced if Benton is unable to play this week. Stay tuned.

Source: Steelers Depot

item.title: Jalen Ramsey (wrist) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Jalen Ramsey PIT Cornerback

Ramsey has a fracture in his wrist. He logged two limited sessions to close out the week. The Buccaneers’ passing attack is hardly imposing with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined, but the Steelers would surely love to have Ramsey out there.

Source: Steelers Depot

item.title: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Tre' Harris LAC Wide Receiver

He did not practice this week and Jim Harbaugh called him “week to week.” Harris stands a chance at returning after Los Angeles’ Week 7 bye.

item.title: Quentin Johnston (chest) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Quentin Johnston LAC Wide Receiver

Stark difference from last week’s limited-limited-rule out. Jim Harbaugh would not commit to putting it on the record that Johnston would be on a snap count. Playing through the injury with Los Angeles’ sad sack offensive line would seem to have Johnston as more of a sketchy FLEX play than a WR3.

item.title: Rico Dowdle (toe) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

Dowdle seemingly has a good chance to play. He was limited on Wednesday, but practiced in full on Thursday and Friday. However, Jaylen Warren has played extremely well with Dowdle sidelined and coach Mike McCarthy has said that Warren will remain a high-volume player. If active, Dowdle is a FLEX starter.

Source: Steelers Depot

item.title: Ladd McConkey (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said he did not know if McConkey or Quentin Johnston would be on snap counts on Sunday. Cool. What we do know is that the Chargers desperately need a win and McConkey is their best receiver, so the incentives are certainly aligned to get McConkey into the fantasy WR3 discussion even with a pitch count.

item.title: Joe Alt (neck) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Joe Alt LAC Tackle

Alt was off to see a specialist, per Jim Harbaugh, on Monday. He did not practice. At this point an IR stint seems more likely than not. The four rookie line should be intact for the Chargers this week with Kayode Awosika also ruled out.

item.title: Steelers ruled out Roman Wilson (finger) for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Roman Wilson PIT Wide Receiver

ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported earlier this week that Wilson was going to miss a couple of weeks, so this is not breaking news. The Steelers’ wide receiver corps is very thin. DK Metcalf (illness) is now questionable to play. Germie Bernard should be in fantasy lineups this week.

Source: Steelers Depot

item.title: DK Metcalf (illness) is questionable for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

This is unfortunate. The Steelers placed Michael Pittman on injured reserve recently, and both Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek are out this week. Metcalf has a chance to play this week, but fantasy managers must, unfortunately, keep an eye on the news over the next 48 hours. Rookie Germie Bernard could lead the team in targets again this week.

Source: Steelers Depot

item.title: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton Jr. (hamstring) is getting “closer” but won’t play in Las Vegas’ Week 6 game against the Bills.
item.description:
Dont'e Thornton LV Wide Receiver

Thornton is in Week 2 of his 21-day window and figures to return in Week 7 or Week 8. Obviously there’s not much reason to trust him in fantasy at this time, but he may find a real role on Las Vegas’ depth chart.

item.title: Jalen Nailor (concussion) will play in Las Vegas’ Week 6 game against the Bills.
item.description:
Jalen Nailor LV Wide Receiver

This per coach Klint Kubiak, so we assume Nailor has passed protocol. He’s only a FLEX play at this point as it’s hard to trust any weapons in the Vegas offense beyond Brock Bowers, even in a good matchup against a struggling Bills defense.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 6 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

Bears coach Ben Johnson said Monangai is “trending in the right direction,” but remains week-to-week. D’Andre Swift should handle a sizable workload with Monangai sidelined. Roschon Johnson may be able to catch a few passes, but he makes for a shaky FLEX bet. Monangai should be stashed safely on fantasy football benches.

Source: Chicago Bears

item.title: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

The Bears are smartly taking a conservative approach with their franchise quarterback. Williams had a limited practice session last week and practiced fully this week. Bears coach Ben Johnson told reporters that the team should have more clarity by the end of the day on whether Williams has passed his return-to-play plan’s final stress tests. Stay tuned.

Source: Courtney R. Cronin

item.title: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Jawhar Jordan will be elevated off the practice squad to play against the Jaguars on Sunday.
item.description:
Jawhar Jordan HOU Running Back

Though he’s nominally the third back with David Montgomery out, the Texans tipped how they felt about Dare Ogunbowale as a running back by not using him a single time after Montgomery was ruled out against the Titans in Week 5. It seems likely that Jordan will be the main Woody Marks change-up in London, though given how poorly the Texans have ran the ball this year that probably doesn’t equate to much fantasy equity.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Giants coach John Harbaugh said “We’ll see. We’ll find out,” when asked if the Giants have reached the point where he’ll make adjustments due to the team’s fumbling issues.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Giants beat writer Dan Duggan chimed in with “I would be very surprised if [Cam] Skattebo has the same RB1 workload on Sunday that he’s had in the first five games.” Skattebo has put the ball on the ground four times in the first five games. Najee Harris has one in 27 carries and Tyrone Tracy has added two. It sounds like Harris may start to be a significant thorn in the side of Skattebo-reliant managers.

Source: Dan Duggan

item.title: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Trent McDuffie

McDuffie reportedly injured his groin during Thursday’s practice, and is now questionable to play. Frankly, the Rams can probably get by without their No. 1 cornerback this week, though obviously it would be preferable to have him out there. Stay tuned.

Source: Adam Grosbard

item.title: Josh Simmons (back) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 6 game against the Chargers.
item.description:
Josh Simmons KC Tackle

Simmons did actually practice this week, so he’s trending in the right direction, but Khalil Benson gets another start while Simmons tries to get past a bulging disc in his back.

Source: Nate Taylor

item.title: Buccaneers ruled out Antoine Winfield (ribs) for Week 6 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Antoine Winfield TB Safety

Winfield’s absence is consequential. The centerfield prowler makes an impact when he is in the game. The Steelers should have a slightly easier time moving the ball against the Buccaneers this week.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Rashee Rice (hamstring) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 6 game against the Chargers.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

It seems like Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce will be getting Only Game In Town treatment against the Chargers, with Cyrus Allen and Jalen Royals also in the mix at wideout now that Rice and Tyquan Thornton are both out. Andy Reid said Rice is “wanting to jump in on everything” but he did not practice this week. He has to be regarded as questionable for Week 7.

Source: Matt Derrick

item.title: FOX Sports’ Greg Auman reports that Sean Tucker (quad) will be a pregame decision for Week 6 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Sean Tucker TB Running Back

We expect to see Tucker officially listed as questionable to play when the injury report drops later today. If he ends up being inactive, that is good news for Bucky Irving, who handled 23 touches last week, ceding seven to Kenny Gainwell and five to Tucker. Irving warrants borderline RB1/2 treatment at this time.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Alvin Kamara (back) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 6 game against the Giants.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

Kamara practiced each day this week, so it’s a bit surprising to see him here. Assuming no rough quotes or reports come out, we’d regard him as on the optimistic side of questionable. He’s a reasonable FLEX play against the Giants.

item.title: Chris Olave (illness) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 6 game against the Giants.
item.description:
Chris Olave NO Wide Receiver

Olave missed the first two days of practice this week with the illness, but we’d ultimately still expect him to play. He should be regarded as on the optimistic side of questionable. He’ll be an easy WR1, assuming he plays, against the Giants in Week 6.

Source: Katherine Terrell

item.title: Cam Jurgens (concussion) will not play in Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
item.description:
Cam Jurgens BAL Center

Jurgens has now missed each of his first two weeks with the Ravens as he tries to shake a brain injury he suffered while with the Eagles. Vega Ioane will likely man center again.

Source: Jonas Shaffer

item.title: Tytus Howard (knee) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Tytus Howard CLE Tackle

His Wednesday DNP suggested worse, but Howard will try to play through the knee injury that cost him roughly half of Cleveland’s snaps against the Jets last week.

item.title: Denzel Boston (foot) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

He’ll be a usable WR3 against the Ravens this week. Boston has returned at least 41 yards in every start this year while hitting a deep gain seemingly weekly. The 22-year-old should be Cleveland’s No. 1 target again this week.

item.title: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Rams.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

The Cardinals officially ruled Love out for this Sunday’s game against the Rams after he was. DNP in practice all week. Head coach Matt LaFleur said Love is not considered a candidate to be placed on injured reserve at this time, but the fact that he even has to mention that is cause for some concern that Love could be looking at a multi-week absence. LaFleur also added that Love’s lack of involvement in the passing game is due to his inability to run routes on his injured ankle. His practice status will be one to monitor next week when the Cardinals begin preparing for the Broncos. Tyler Allgeier should be in line for a busy day against the Rams and will be a volume-based RB2 play.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Browns coach Todd Monken said KC Concepcion (concussion) has cleared protocol and will play in Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
KC Concepcion KC Concepcion

Concepcion will have some low-end WR3/FLEX appeal with four teams on bye in PPR leagues. He simply hasn’t been able to find much space with his opportunities so far, with two 25-yard catches and 16 other catches that went for just 99 yards in his first five weeks of action.

item.title: Carson Schwesinger (ankle) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
Carson Schwesinger CLE Linebacker

Schwesinger played through a high-ankle sprain last year, so we anticipate he’s more likely to be active than not after returning to practice today. The second-year star linebacker will likely attempt to power through against the Ravens.

item.title: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Browns.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Jackson will miss a second straight game with his ankle injury despite reports at the beginning of the week that said he had a “realistic” chance to play in Week 6. It was also reported after the team’s overtime win against the Falcons that Lamar was “closer than people realized” to playing in Week 5. Jackson and the Ravens will now set their sights on having him ready to go in Week 7 at home against the Bengals, while Tyler Huntley will draw the start this week against the Browns.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
Quinshon Judkins CLE Running Back

He only got in a limited session on Friday, leaving us to conclude this is likely a true questionable situation. The viability of Jaleel McLaughlin as a FLEX play will probably be determined by if Judkins is active or not. It’s also possible Judkins plays on a pitch count. He’ll be a shaky low-end RB2 if active.

item.title: Dylan Sampson (knee) won’t play in Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
Dylan Sampson CLE Running Back

Sampson practiced each of the last two days, but it was too little, too late, for Week 6. He stands a chance at returning in Week 7. As long as Quinshon Judkins is relatively healthy, Sampson won’t have standalone value.

item.title: A.J. Brown (ankle) is questionable for New England’s Week 6 game against the Jets.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said they’d make the decision on whether to activate him off injured reserve on Saturday, so at least Brown won’t be a game-time decision. Brown can be started with confidence if he’s active, though he’d potentially be in line for a pitch count to the point where he’d be more of a WR2 than a WR1 in his return.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Michael Penix has been removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bears.
item.description:
Michael Penix ATL Quarterback

It was reported the day after the Falcons’ overtime loss to the Ravens that there was “optimism” that Penix would start in Week 6. After being upgraded to a full participant on Thursday’s practice, he seemed like a lock to be ready to go by Sunday, so Friday’s news isn’t all that unexpected. Penix has thrown for 719 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception this season, throwing one touchdown in each of his first three games. He’ll be on the fantasy radar in 2QB/Superflex leagues against a Bears defense that has allowed just two top-12 fantasy finishes to opposing QBs this season.

Source: Tori McElhaney

item.title: Monroe Freeling (knee) is doubtful for Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
item.description:
Monroe Freeling CAR OFFENSIVE TACKLE (SUB)

The rookie got in back-to-back limited sessions, but they must have indeed been quite limited for him to wind up with the rarely-used doubtful tag. It’s very unlikely he plays this weekend. Taylor Moton (blood clot) is questionable after three full practices and would seem to be the favorite to start at right tackle.

item.title: Darren Waller (toe) is not on Carolina’s final Week 6 injury report.
item.description:
Darren Waller CAR Tight End

He upgraded to a full practice today. Waller will be a low-end TE2 with Jalen Coker (quad) playing in Week 6 against a Jalen Hurts-less Eagles outfit.

item.title: Trevor Etienne (ankle) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
item.description:
Trevor Etienne CAR Running Back

Panthers coach Dave Canales said Etienne would be activated off injured reserve for this week. Etienne practiced in full all week and, with AJ Dillon ruled out, the Panthers currently have just one healthy back on the 53-man roster. Perhaps he’ll be joined by a practice squad player as well. Either way, Etienne has no stand-alone value this week.

item.title: AJ Dillon (ankle) will not play in Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
item.description:
AJ Dillon CAR Running Back

He didn’t practice all week. With Jonathon Brooks also out, it seems likely that Trevor Etienne will be activated to serve as Chuba Hubbard’s main backup. Hubbard will project to get most of the volume here and has stumbled into high-end RB2 value this week.

item.title: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said it’s “too early to tell” if Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be able to play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield has already been ruled out for Week 6’s game against the Steelers. After being a DNP in practice all week, Mayfield could still be another week away from returning. It was reported on Wednesday that he is still unable to grip/throw a football, so this will be a situation to keep an eye on when the Bucs begin prepping for next week’s game.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Stefon Diggs WAS Wide Receiver

After missing all of practice last week and being a DNP on Thursday, Diggs was back on the field Friday, which is a good sign for his Week 6 availability with one practice left to go in the week. The Commanders take on the 49ers on Monday Night Football this week and will likely announce Diggs’ availability sometime Saturday, but he could be on track to return in what is a must-win game for the 1-3-1 Commanders. Diggs has caught 18 passes for 170 yards and three touchdowns this season and would be in the mix as a fringe WR3/WR4 if active.

Source: John Keim

item.title: Lamar Jackson (ankle) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

All signs are pointing to Tyler Huntley making his second straight start. Jackson was a DNP for all three practices this week and will likely be ruled out in the next few hours, meaning Huntley will have a chance at a “revenge game” against a Browns team that he spent part of the 2024 and 2025 seasons with. Huntley threw for 201-2-0 in last week’s win over the Falcons and rushed for another 20 yards and one touchdown. He’ll have some appeal in 2QB and Superflex leagues on the road against the Browns.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) returned to practice on Friday.
item.description:
Quinshon Judkins CLE Running Back

This is an improvement for Judkins, who was a DNP for the team’s first two practices this week. Head coach Todd Monken said earlier this week that Judkins was considered day-to-day, so we’ll see if he has a shot at playing when the team releases its final injury report in a couple of hours. It seems unlikely that Judkins will be fully removed from the injury report, meaning he’ll likely carry a questionable designation heading into the weekend.

Source: Mary Kay Cabot

item.title: Kevin Winston (undisclosed) will not play in Week 6 against the Colts.
item.description:
Kevin Winston TEN Safety

Winston has been a DNP in practice all week and has now been ruled out for Week 6’s game against the Colts. The second-year safety has started all four games he has appeared in this season, totaling 29 tackles and one forced fumble while earning a PFF coverage grade of 47.2.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Eagles signed Joe Milton, formerly of the Cowboys.
item.description:
Joe Milton PHI Quarterback

Milton will join Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton on the Eagles’ 53-man roster. This move comes a day after it was revealed that Jalen Hurts would be out indefinitely due to a superficial blood clot that could sideline him for the next several weeks. Milton will likely serve as the Eagles’ emergency third QB on game days and seems unlikely to see any playing time at this point.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Omar Cooper Jr. will play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

Cooper had his 21-day practice window opened earlier this week, but is officially set to return after logging a full practice on Friday. The rookie receiver could step into an immediate role for the Jets with Adonai Mitchell (finger) out for at least one more week, but he could still be a few weeks away from fantasy relevance. Cooper played on just five snaps in Week 1 before his injury, but did catch one pass for 30 yards.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Adonai Mitchell NYJ Wide Receiver

It was reported earlier this week that Mitchell underwent a “small procedure” on the finger he injured in practice ahead of Week 3. Given that news, it doesn’t come as much of a surprise to learn that Mitchell will miss his fourth straight game with the injury. With rookie Omar Cooper Jr. set to play in his first game since Week 1, Mitchell could face additional competition for targets when he finally returns to the field.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

Things have been trending in this direction for Hall all week. The 25-year-old back was a DNP on both Wednesday and Thursday, and will now miss a third straight game as a result of his injury. Braelon Allen will again lead the Jets’ backfield this week against the Patriots and has handled 44 of the Jets’ 48 running back opportunities since Week 4. Allen will be a volatile RB2 against a Patriots defense that ranks 18th against running backs in fantasy scoring this season.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-3 targets for 19 yards in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
item.description:
Courtland Sutton DEN Wide Receiver

Nix’s only incompletion when targeting Sutton resulted in the veteran receiver getting rocked over the middle of the field on a ball Nix led him directly into oncoming contact. Sutton vented his frustration by repeatedly pounding the ground following the hit, with it unclear whether it was due to the hit or the incompletion on third down on a night the Broncos struggled to move the football to the tune of only 168 yards of total offense. Fantasy managers likely aren’t utilizing Sutton as a weekly option, but will want to track his practice status ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Cardinals if bye week fill-ins are required.

item.title: RJ Harvey rushed six times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks, adding 31 yards on three receptions.
item.description:
RJ Harvey DEN Running Back

The fact that the 31 yards through the air led the team in receiving is a comment on the state of an offense that gained only 168 yards of total offense against the defending Super Bowl Champions. Even so, a relentlessly aggressive defense willed the team to victory behind a consistently positive game script, which allowed J.K. Dobbins to handily lead the backfield in opportunities. Harvey remains a matchup-dependent fantasy option best utilized in trailing game environments, which is unlikely to be the case when the Broncos face the struggling Cardinals in Week 7.

item.title: J.K. Dobbins rushed 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
item.description:
J.K. Dobbins DEN Running Back

Dobbins found little room to run on a night the Broncos gained only 168 yards of total offense but handily led the backfield in opportunities in what was a consistently positive game script due to the dominance of their defense. Dobbins has now failed to eclipse a modest 50 yards on the ground in four of five appearances but might be useful as a bye week fill-in when the Broncos travel to Arizona to face the Cardinals in Week 7.

item.title: Bo Nix completed 17-of-27 passes for 107 yards in the Broncos’ 17-14, Week 6 win over the Seahawks, adding two yards on four carries.
item.description:
Bo Nix DEN Quarterback

The Broncos managed just 168 yards of total offense on a night their defense carried them to victory in overtime. Nine of the Broncos’ 11 possessions, excluding the two kneel downs to end each half, ended in punts on drives that lasted five plays or fewer. Two second quarter touchdown drives had the Broncos playing with a lead for much of the game but they were otherwise unable to move the football with any consistency. An overtime interception by nickel corner Ja’Quan McMillian allowed for a game-winning, 53-yard field goal from kicker Will Lutz after the Broncos again failed to gain a first down. The win sends Denver to 4-2 while averaging only 18.7 points per game through six weeks. The team gets a scheduling gift with the Cardinals on deck in Week 7, although Nix cannot be treated as a starter-worthy fantasy asset outside of the deepest leagues.

item.title: Cooper Kupp caught 5-of-10 targets for 50 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Cooper Kupp SEA Wide Receiver

Kupp’s 10 targets finished second on the team behind alpha Jaxon Smith-Njigba but were largely a product of 51 Sam Darnold pass attempts in game that had all the ingredients for increased pass volume, including an inability to run the football, negative game script, and overtime. It continues to appear as if Kupp’s fantasy-relevant days are far behind him, with the veteran best left on the waiver wire ahead of a Week 7 showdown against the Chiefs on deck.

item.title: Rashid Shaheed caught 5-of-8 targets for 66 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos, adding two yards on one carry.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

Shaheed’s eight targets were a product of 51 Sam Darnold pass attempts in a game the Seahawks could not find any room to run on the ground. He lost a fumble on a fluke play in the second quarter in which he rolled over the tackling defender, only for the defender’s knee to knock the football loose before Shaheed’s rear end touched the playing surface. he would fumble a punt return in the fourth quarter but easily had time to regain control before the ball was in real trouble. Shaheed remains the third option through the air for an offense typically not seeing this level of volume, making him a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option, for the time being. That doesn’t change ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Chiefs in Seattle.

item.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12-of-16 targets for 134 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Jaxon Smith-Njigba SEA Wide Receiver

Smith-Njigba overcame a sluggish first half to extend his stranglehold on the overall WR1 in fantasy circles with a dominant second half and overtime period. While the 51 pass attempts from Sam Darnold were highly uncharacteristic of this Seattle offense, a complete inability to run the football paired with a negative script to form the perfect environment for Smith-Njigba to set a season high in targets and receptions. Smith-Njigba has now gone over 100 yards in five of six appearances to start the 2026 regular season and is in a good spot to continue that dominance when the Seahawks host the Chiefs in Week 7, where he remains a top-tier WR1 in fantasy circles.

item.title: George Holani rushed five times for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
George Holani SEA Running Back

Holani split primary change of pace duties with recent practice squad call-up Velus Jones Jr, the latter of whom turned four carries into 20 yards while losing one yard on his lone reception. Both backs appear unlikely to return fantasy value as Zach Charbonnet nears a return from injured reserve.

item.title: Emanuel Wilson rushed 14 times for 52 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Emanuel Wilson SEA Running Back

Wilson is now down to just 3.4 yards per carry while filling in for numerous key injuries in the Seattle backfield, with the team clearly waiting with bated breath for the return of Zach Charbonnet. Charbonnet continues to inch closer to a return from injured reserve and appears likely to bring an end to the Wilson experiment, relegating the latter to bench fodder in fantasy circles in the process. That could come a early a Week 7 when the Seahawks host the Chiefs.

item.title: Sam Darnold completed 27-of-51 passes for 278 yards and two interceptions in the Seahawks’ 17-14, Week 6 loss to the Broncos, adding 19 yards on two carries.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

The Seahawks struggled to move the football throughout against the tenacious situational play calling from Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, scoring only three points until just over five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. A late-game surge saw them punch on in and a successful two-point conversion drew the team within three points. They would stop the Broncos on the subsequent possession but an interception in Denver territory put the game in jeopardy. The defense would do their job and force a three-and-out that took only 15 seconds off the clock, giving the ball back to Darnold to lead a two-minute drill to send the game to overtime through a chip shot field goal. Darnold would throw his second interception in overtime, watching from the sideline as the Broncos walked it off with a 53-yard Will Lutz field goal. The loss sends the Seahawks to 3-3, matching the total number of losses from a season ago through only six weeks of the 2026 season. The Seahawks have work to do to make up ground in the NFC West, now 2.5 games behind the undefeated 49ers through the first third of the regular season. Darnold and the Seahawks now have a long week to prepare for the now-undefeated Chiefs at home in Week 7, where Darnold will be a fringe QB2 in fantasy circles.

item.title: Colts released Darius Slayton.
item.description:
Darius Slayton

Slayton signed with the Colts less than a month ago but never suited up for the team on game day. The 29-year-old speedster was briefly considered as a candidate to replace Alec Pierce (foot), but he’s once again on the open market in search of work. A knee injury resulted in Slayton being scratched from Week 5’s matchup against the Steelers, so it’s possible he’ll have to prove he’s healthy before signing elsewhere this season.

Source: Indianapolis Colts

item.title: Evan Engram caught both targets for 13 yards in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
item.description:
Evan Engram DEN Tight End

Engram has not seen more than five targets in a game this season and has been held out of the end zone since Week 1, making him a difficult start in fantasy leagues of all sizes. He can safely remain on the bench in an enticing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 7.

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) returned to the game in the fourth quarter of Week 6 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Waddle departed in the third quarter and was deemed questionable to return with a shoulder injury but made his way back to the field in the fourth quarter, catching two additional passes in the final frame. He ended with four receptions for 24 yards on seven targets and has quickly become a difficult weekly start in fantasy circles. An enticing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 7 is sure to give fantasy managers a hint of potential, but if he fails again to return a usable fantasy week, it might be time to reconsider entering him in weekly lineups.

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Waddle departed early in the third quarter and was quickly deemed questionable to return with a shoulder injury. It is unclear when the injury occurred. Waddle managed to catch just 2-of-5 targets for 15 yards prior to departing, keeping his usable weeks total at just two games through the first six weeks of the 2026 season. Fantasy managers that invested a fourth-round pick on the veteran wide receiver have got to begin to make alternate plans at wide receiver moving forward.

item.title: Elijah Arroyo (arm) was taken to the locker room in the second quarter of week 6 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Elijah Arroyo SEA Tight End

Arroyo was injured while trying to recover a Rashid Shaheed fumble in the second quarter and was promptly escorted to the locker room with trainers helping to stabilize his arm. It appeared to be a potential wrist or shoulder injury based on how the staff helped him off the field. The second-year tight end was not targeted prior to departing and appears to be on the wrong side of questionable to return to Week 6.

item.title: Brock Bowers (knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

The Raiders continue managing Bowers’ practice reps early in the week, though he plays unrestrictedly on game day. The Raiders face the Bills in Week 6, likely facilitating a fantasy-friendly game environment. Bowers should be treated as the overall TE1 as usual this week.

Source: Paul H. Gutierrez

item.title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Demarcus Robinson (ankle) has an “outside chance” to return in Week 7 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Demarcus Robinson SF Wide Receiver

The 49ers go on bye in Week 8. Shanahan says that Robinson is more likely to return after that, in time to face the Raiders in Week 9. Robinson can be stashed in injured reserve spots, if need be, but he is not a must-stash type of player. Depending on how the 49ers’ wide receiver corps looks, Robinson can likely be snagged off waivers during the bye week for those in need at the wide receiver position.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Davis Allen

Allen remains out, and Parkinson (shoulder) remains limited. Tyler Higbee has played productively in the Rams’ No. 1 tight end role, and he should be expected to do so again this week against the Cardinals.

Source: Bo Brack

item.title: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Tyler Allgeier should be rostered in 10-team leagues. The Cardinals have downplayed Love’s ankle issues, but two missed practices are not a good sign. He still has a chance to suit up in Week 6 against the Rams, but he is currently on the wrong side of questionable.

Source: Bo Brack

item.title: Ashton Jeanty (foot) said he is feeling “great” and “ready to go” for Week 6 against the Bills.
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

The quotes read a tad bit more enthusiastically than Jeanty did while speaking to media members at his locker, but this is still good to hear. Jeanty has been dealing with an ankle injury for a long time, but the team took that injury off the weekly practice report this week. He is now listed only with the foot injury after experiencing “a flare-up of plantar fasciitis” last Friday. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 against the Bills this week.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Seahawks declared LB Drake Thomas, CB Avery Smith, WR Montorie Foster Jr., DT Brandon Pili, QB Jalen Milroe, LB Chazz Surratt and RB Robert Henry inactive for Week 6 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Drake Thomas SEA Linebacker

Thomas is dealing with an ankle injury and needs more time to get healthy. The Seahawks recently signed Henry, a rookie, but evidently he will not play this evening, despite the Seahawks’ running back group being a tad thin due to injuries. The Seahawks face the Broncos on Thursday Night Football.

Source: Gregg Bell

item.title: Riley Moss (ribs) is active for Week 6 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Riley Moss DEN Cornerback

Moss, one of the Broncos’ starting cornerbacks, returns from a one-game absence. He injured his ribs in Week 4 against the 49ers. The Broncos declared QB Sam Ehlinger, OL Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, DL Jordan Jackson and DL Tyler Onyedim inactive for Week 6 against the Seahawks. Ehlinger will serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Terry McLaurin WAS Wide Receiver

McLaurin posted a 4/62 receiving line, playing through this hamstring injury in Week 5 against the Giants. Kicking off the week with a limited session is a great sign for his Week 6 availability and overall health. Expect McLaurin to be even more involved against the 49ers on Monday night.

Source: Washington Commanders

item.title: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Austin Ekeler WAS Running Back

Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Will Campbell (knee) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Will Campbell NE OFFENSIVE TACKLE (SUB)

The Patriots’ left tackle seemingly has a chance to play in Week 6 against the Jets. According to Mass Live’s Mark Daniels, Campbell “was out here moving well in full pads,” and lined up with the starters during the portion of practice open to the media. This is great news for Drake Maye.

Source: Mark Daniels

item.title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he’s “hoping Nick Bosa (calf) can go” in Week 6 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive Lineman

Unfortunately, Bosa has not yet resumed practicing, though the 49ers have an extra day to let Bosa rehab. They face the Commanders in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Late last week, Bosa told reporters that it is “pretty darn likely” he plays in Week 6. Stay tuned.

Source: Matt Barrows

item.title: Joshua Palmer (shoulder) was seen practicing in a red non-contact jersey on Thursday.
item.description:
Joshua Palmer BUF Wide Receiver

This is a good first step, but Palmer may need another week or so off before he returns to the field. Palmer injured his shoulder in practice last week and was unable to face the Rams in Week 5.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: DJ Moore (shoulder) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

It looks like the Bills could again be without their No. 1 wide receiver on game day. Josh Allen and Co. take on the Raiders this weekend, in what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment. Hopefully, Moore resumes practicing soon.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Ed Oliver (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Ed Oliver BUF Defensive Lineman

The Bills’ stud defensive tackle is on the wrong side of questionable for the Bills’ Week 6 game against the Raiders. Fortunately, the pass rush is playing very effectively despite Oliver’s continued injury issues.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Joe Alt (neck) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Joe Alt LAC Tackle

Chargers OG Kayode Awosika (fibula), S Derwin James (hamstring) and CB Donte Jackson (hamstring) also remained sidelined. The Chargers take on the division-rival Chiefs this weekend.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Ladd McConkey (foot) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey is on track to once again be active on game day, but it is unclear how involved he will be. Two limited sessions are a good sign, but it would be great to see him practice fully tomorrow. In that instance, starting him as a WR2 would be far more palatable.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Quentin Johnston LAC Wide Receiver

Johnston is on track to play, but this wide receiver corps is very banged up. KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and Brenen Thompson (quad) remained limited as well. Marquez Valdes-Scantling (ribs) upgraded to full.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Drew Kendall (knee) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Drew Kendall PHI Center

The Eagles’ starting center now has a chance to play in Week 6 against the Panthers. Eagles LG Landon Dickerson (knee) was also limited again, as was EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle).

item.title: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Wicks played through the hamstring injury in Week 5 and may have made it worse. Downgrading to a DNP on Thursday is a bad sign. He is unlikely to play at this time, and if active, he would be prone to re-injury.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for his team’s Week 6 game against the Panthers, potentially leaving Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue to split touches. Hopefully, reports clarify whether Pierce would handle a sizable workload as the de facto starter.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo said he is “still hearing optimism he’ll play Sunday. We’ll see.” Given his follow-up comment, it doesn’t seem like he shares the organization’s optimism. If active, Smith would be catching passes thrown by backup Tanner McKee. Jalen Hurts is sidelined indefinitely by a blood clot. McKee, a pocket passer, could lock onto Smith, keeping him in the WR2 tier if active.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Texans ruled out Tank Dell (knee) for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Tank Dell HOU Wide Receiver

The Texans depart for London tonight to face the Jaguars on Sunday, and Dell will remain in Texas. He is currently practicing in full, but the team has not yet cleared him for game-day activities. Dell does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Texans ruled out David Montgomery (groin) for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
David Montgomery HOU Running Back

We already knew that Montgomery was considered week-to-week, so this is unsurprising. Woody Marks will start for however long Montgomery is sidelined. The Jaguars field one of the NFL’s best run defenses, but Marks ceded just one snap to Dare Ogunbowale last week. Theoretically, he should remain in a near-full-time role, elevating him to the RB2/FLEX tier despite the tough matchup.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that returning in Week 8 against the Chiefs is more likely for Pat Surtain (ankle) than in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Pat Surtain DEN Cornerback

Palmer also clarified that Surtain did not suffer a non-contact injury, as has been reported previously. Surtain apparently injured his ankle two plays before he exited the Broncos’ Week 5 game against the 49ers. The Broncos might be able to get by without Surtain next week, but getting him back before facing Patrick Mahomes would be huge.

Source: James Palmer

item.title: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Cam Jurgens BAL Center

Jurgens still has a chance to play, but we had hoped to see him upgrade to full participation. Ravens EDGE Mike Green (hamstring) was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. Ravens OG Andrew Vorhees (foot) joins him in the limited column. Ravens RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) upgraded to full participation. Ravens OG John Simpson (groin) downgraded to a DNP.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

Rice strained his hamstring in Week 4. Although Chiefs coach Andy Reid initially said Rice only “tweaked” it, The Athletic’s Mike Silver reported a few hours later that Rice could be out for several weeks. The fact that Rice remains sidelined for the first two practices following his team’s Week 5 bye is a bad sign. He is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6 against the Chargers. If he can get in a limited session tomorrow, that could put him on track to play in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

Bateman played through the shoulder injury last week. He was limited yesterday, but coach Jesse Minter said he wasn’t worried. Downgrading to a DNP is not a good sign. Meanwhile, Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing fully this week and could hop right into WR2 duties for the Ravens.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Tytus Howard (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Tytus Howard CLE Tackle

It’s good progress after he had a Wednesday DNP. Howard should have a real chance at playing on Sunday as long as his Friday status stays neutral or trends positively.

item.title: Zay Flowers (toe) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Flowers played through a foot injury last week, catching 8-of-9 targets for 53 yards and rushing once for 13 yards. This injury could be related, but we really don’t know. Flowers’ productivity took a hit with Tyler Huntley running the offense last week. Huntley is currently in line to start again, though Lamar Jackson’s (ankle) status is still up in the air. If the toe injury limits Flowers, that further complicates things, but he still must be started if active. Hopefully, he practices tomorrow.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Dylan Sampson CLE Running Back

This is at least some positive momentum towards being activated and helping the Browns out on Sunday, though even if Sampson was activated he’d likely be in a committee. We’ll see what Friday brings, but unless it’s a full session, we’d be surprised if Sampson was more than a sketchy questionable for Week 6.

item.title: KC Concepcion (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
KC Concepcion KC Concepcion (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.

He’s still in concussion protocol, but it looks like he’ll have at least some chance of clearing before Sunday’s game against the Ravens. Concepcion would struggle to be more than a FLEX option here even if healthy, so fantasy managers should probably look at alternatives this week.
item.rw:position: Concepcion (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.

item.title: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

Of the (many) Browns in real danger of missing this week’s game against the Ravens, Boston seems to be in the best shape of actually playing. Still, it is two limited sessions in two tries and we wouldn’t be surprised if he wound up with a questionable tag on Friday.

item.title: Lamar Jackson (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
